Welcome to America’s biggest and busiest Indian Pakistani restaurant, where over 4,000 people eat every day! 

Aga's Restaurant (https://maps.app.goo.gl/4YG4VbeNHMr3sJuNA) in Houston, Texas has an incredible story, started by a family with roots in both India and Pakistan. Today, it’s one of the greatest restaurants outside of India and Pakistan, and it’s story of united people from across the world to eat delicious food, and hospitality in the heart of Houston, Texas. 

I was privileged to to meet Mr. Shaukat Maredia, learn a little about the story of Aga's Restaurant. 

But how was the food? After getting a full tour of the kitchen and trying 18 of their best dishes, I can safely say it’s some of the best Indian and Pakistani food I’ve had outside of India and Pakistan! 

When you’re in Houston, Texas, Aga's Restaurant is mandatory!

Today we’re going on an ultimate Texas BBQ tour in Houston! We’ll try three different places for the best craft bbq, the best historical bbq, and a place that’s serving amazing fusion bbq. Houston has some of the most underrated BBQ in Texas! 

Pinkerton's Barbecue (https://maps.app.goo.gl/pjhErKynMfZZahtF8) - First up is Pinkerton's Barbecue where we met up with owner Grant Pinkerton. Pinkerton’s has a Bib Gourmand from the Michelin Guide, and they serve up some up the highest rated BBQ in Houston. The beef ribs, brisket, pork ribs, sausages and sides were all phenomenal. 

Pizzitola’s Heritage BBQ (https://maps.app.goo.gl/E4Zps9h2R2HZdj8b6) - Next up we met up with Tim Taylor from Pizzitola’s Heritage BBQ to see the old bbq pits that are one of a kind in Houston. The ribs were extraordinary, for any BBQ lover it’s something you have  to try, and I also really loved their sauce. 

Brisket & Rice (https://maps.app.goo.gl/7sMFnvzqo1DFtxxQA) - Next we met up with brothers Hong Tran and Phong Tran to try Brisket & Rice where they make Texas BBQ but with a twist of their Vietnamese roots. Their brisket fried rice is amazing, and you also can’t miss their ribs, and brisket!

Some people say the best food in New Orleans is hidden in the back of gas stations and convenience stores, so today our mission is to put it to the test and taste some of the highest rated gas station food in New Orleans, Louisiana!

John & Mary Food Store (https://maps.app.goo.gl/1bvJ9HmQUcUVY9mS9) - This is a great place to come for Yakamein. 

Banks Meat Market (https://maps.app.goo.gl/Q8sZ48tHE7SVGfaN6) - This place is legendary in New Orleans for their 24 hour gas station food including their 32 Inch Hot Sausage Po' Boy. 

Broad & Banks Seafood (https://maps.app.goo.gl/Xb2TWtamotRdFDZVA) - Another gem of New Orleans, I tried their legendary Gumbo, Smothered Pork Chops, and Red Beans and Rice.

Hanks Seafood & Supermarket (https://maps.app.goo.gl/eDqmpSxRZYH8NpCG8) - Another top recommendation, and we tried the roast beef po’ boy, another hot sausage po’ boy, and a classic fried shrimp po’ boy. Welcome to New Orleans, Louisiana, one of the greatest food destinations in the United States! Today we’re going to Castnet Seafood, one of the best seafood restaurants and seafood wholesalers in New Orleans - it's the source for the best seafood in the city! 

I arrived a little early and met up with Tom who showed me around Castnet, everything from the fresh oyster being shucked to the fish of the day. 

But definitely the highlight is the fresh crawfish, a food that’s seasonal and loved throughout Louisiana. First they have to sort and clean all the crawfish. Then they go into a boil, which is loaded with their own secret seasoning, lemons, onions, and celery. The crawfish need to boil, then they are soaked in the juice to absorb as much of it as possible. 

I tried their crawfish boil which was loaded with flavor and a good kick of spice. Then I had some shrimp, crabs, corn, gumbo, and a fried shrimp poboy. All the food was fantastic. 

If you’re looking for the best seafood in New Orleans, go to Castnet Seafood!

XmMoGRI0k2c.description:
It’s Ramadan, and tonight we’re going on an Indian street food tour in Old Delhi. But first, we’re having Iftar (evening meal breaking the fast) at Jama Masjid in the heart of Old Delhi! Huge thank you to Anubhav Sapra @delhifoodwalks for arranging this amazing tour! 

Jama Masjid - We’re starting at Jama Masjid where every evening during Ramadan over 30,000 people gather for Iftar, which is the meal after sunset during Ramadan. It was a beautiful moment, sitting together with 30,000 people sharing dates, fruits, samosas, and pakoras. 

Qureshi Kabab Corner - After Jama Masjid, we hit the streets of Old Delhi, an Indian street food paradise. First up for some of the best seekh kebabs at Qureshi Kabab Corner. 

Karim Hotel - You can’t go on a food tour to Old Delhi without paying tribute to Karim Hotel, an institution. And Anubhav and I tried Chicken Burra, Brain Curry, Mutton Korma, and Chicken Ishtoo.

Aslam Chicken - For one of the world’s most buttery butter chicken you have to go to Aslam. They grill their chicken, then drench it in yoghurt and cream, sprinkle it with masala, and submerge it in melted butter.

Haji Mohd. Hussain - This is one of the most legendary places to eat in Old Delhi, and their fried chicken is triple fried to give it insane crispiness, sprinkled in masala, and served with a tangy chutney. 

Taufiq Biryani - Next up on our Indian street food tour we tried Delhi Biryani, my first time to try this style. It was all about the pickle achar that gave it so much flavor. 

Meetha Samosa - Finally, another Ramadan sweet snack is a sweet samosa filled with mild solids. 

Ramadan is a special time in Old Delhi, and Iftar at Jama Masjid along with extreme Indian street food in Old Delhi was an incredible experience! 

Go check out Anubhav's channel: https://www.youtube.com/@delhifoodwalks

Welcome to Taste of Texas, one of the biggest and busiest steakhouses in the United States! Today we’ll be getting a behind the scene look into how they serve over 1000 steak a day to thousands of happy customers and why this steakhouse is so legendary! 

I’m hanging out with my friend Steven and Christina from Houston’s Got Spice: https://www.instagram.com/houstonsgotspice/

Opened since 1977, by the amazing Edd and Nina Hendee, Taste of Texas is an American food institution, and it’s more than just a steakhouse, it’s also a museum of Texas history. Today they are the largest independent user of Certified Angus Beef in the world.

We couldn’t decide which steak to order so we got the 38 oz. dino Texas tomahawk and a giant fillet wrapped in bacon. 

Additionally, Taste of Texas is famous for their traditional American style salad bar which is one of the best salad bars you’ll ever try. 

And don’t forget their Texas sized desserts, the snickers pie was absolutely delicious.

Shout out to Austin, our server, who did an incredible job!

Today we’re exploring Iraqi Kurdistan and the incredible city of Erbil! It’s a city with thousands of years of history that all surround the ancient citadel in the center of the city. 

Machko Cafe - We’re starting with breakfast at this amazing and historical cafe for the full Kurdish breakfast including lots of tea. 

Yassin Kebab - If there’s one place you have to eat kebabs when you’re in Erbil, it must be Yassin Kebab, loved by both locals and visitors, and known for serving some of the best kebabs in Iraq. 

After the amazing kebabs we walked around the old center of Erbil, had some Kurdish Coffee (made from the terebinth tree), tried some Iraqi tree gum, and couldn’t miss some freshly squeezed pomegranate juice.   

Habeeb Kurdish Restaurant - Located on the famous Iskan Street food street, I was able to try some traditional Kurdish food including some amazing dolma!

Iskan Street - Iskan street in Erbil is famous for its night street food and I tried a few different sandwiches and some of the best chickpeas ever! 

Erbil is an amazing city! 

Make sure you check out Epic Food Journeys on Nat Geo now: https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLeoy0zUu6bqm55BdqGDq6HWT02eBSg2hi&si=79f0JBDN5xGcJfSJ

Today we’re going on an ultimate 24 hour Iraqi street food tour in Baghdad. We’re starting with one of the craziest breakfasts in the world, and wait till you see all the other amazing Iraqi food we’re about to eat. 

8 AM Rasul Kahi Geymar - Welcome to the ultimate Iraqi breakfast in Baghdad, called kahi geymar, a flaky pastry bread, soaked in syrup, topped with geymar buffalo cream and pistachio.  

9 AM Sajad Abo Oruk - Just down the road we headed to the next spot, a Baghdad street food stall specializing in a different type of Iraqi breakfast. We tried Bagela bil Dihin - Fava beans and fat, and Makhlama - Iraqi omelet. 

12 PM Iraqi Martyr Monument - Next up with did a little sightseeing in Baghdad before our next meal. 

1 PM Abo Hamza Restaurant - Located in the back alleys of Al-Kazimiyya Mosque, this restaurant serves amazing home-style Iraqi food.

2 PM Al-Kazimiyya Mosque - This is a place you have to visit when you’re in Baghdad. 

4 PM Haidar Double Falafel - How is Iraqi falafel? We’re about to find out by going to try the best Iraqi falafel in Baghdad. 

5 PM al-Tahrir Square, Baghdad, Iraq  

6 PM Haji Raheem Kebab - You can’t come to Baghdad without trying Iraqi kebabs, probably one of the most popular foods in Iraq, and Ahmed took me to this amazing street stall. 

8 PM Maslawi Pacha - Another incredible Iraqi dish is known as Pacha - sheep head and organs, and the fried mumbar - intestines stuffed with rice - was on another level! 

A huge thank you to Ahmed and Aya from https://enliltravels.com/ for arranging my trip to Iraq.

What’s it like to spend 24 hours at the Winter Olympics? And how’s the food? Thank you to The @Olympics and @YouTube for inviting me to the Winter Olympics - Milano Cortina 2026! 

I traveled to Milan, then took a 4.5 hour van ride into the beautiful mountains of Livigno in the Italian Alps for the Games. 

In this video I’ll show you what it’s like to spend a full day at the Winter Olympics in Livigno, starting with morning wakeup, breakfast, and a quick room tour. We also got an exclusive behind the scenes tour to the top of the big air ski jump for the view. I’ll show you all the food I ate for lunch at the Olympic Hospitality. 

Another highlight was getting to chat with Pat Burgener, a professional snowboarder and musician at the Olympics - and it was cool to hear his response to “what an Olympic athlete eats?” 

Finally, you can’t come to Italy without trying some of the local traditional Italian food, and I was excited to try Pizzoccheri, Tzigoiner, and Salmì di cervo. An amazing meal! 

It was an incredible day at the Winter Olympics 2026! 

Thank you again to The Olympics and YouTube. #MilanoCortina2026 #invitedbyyoutube

Welcome to Baghdad, Iraq! Today we’re eating the best Iraqi street food in Baghdad! 

A huge thank you to Ahmet and Aya from https://enliltravels.com/ for arranging my trip to Iraq.

Kubba Saray - We’re starting in Old Baghdad to try a unique version of kubba from an old shop tucked within the book and school market. 

Shabandar Café - Located on the iconic Mutanabbi Street in Baghdad, you’ll find the oldest teahouse. And I tried Nooma Basri, a dried lime tea. Afterwards, just outside I ate some classic winter Iraqi street foods including chickpeas and turnips. 

Bourek Taha - Just down the road you’ll find Bourek Taha that has served the Iraqi version of bourek for generations. 

Mr. Garbage Raisin Juice - This place is legendary and their raisin juice hits the spot. 

Abu Hussein Iraqi Gus - Just about every country in the Middle East has their own version of shawarma, and every version is a little different. Gus is the Iraqi version of shawarma, and I was very curious to see how it tasted. 

Al Qameh Restaurant - For lunch in Baghdad, Ahemet took me to one of his favorite spots for a mix of homestyle Iraqi dishes and stews including lamb quzi. 

Baghdadi Restaurant - But of all the amazing Iraqi foods, Masgouf is the king of them all, a slow roasted freshwater carp fish, standing vertically with a blazing fire. This is one of the world’s greatest fire grilling bbq techniques. 

Hamooqy - Finally, we headed to Hamooqy, a legendary Iraqi street food vendor to try his unique meatballs and omelets.

Today we’re going on an ultimate South African food tour in Cape Town, South Africa where we’ll eat the best gatsby and find out what Cape Malay food really is! 

Super Fisheries - We’re starting this Cape Town food tour today in Athlone to try the original Gatsby, a giant fast food creation that is one of the most well known street foods in Cape Town and this is where they invented it. I enjoyed their amazing Calamari, Fish and Chips Gatsby. Price - 180 ZAR ($10.72)

Arshad's Kitchen - Next up we’re heading to Arshad's Kitchen to try some of the best chicken tikka in Cape Town, and they serve amazing Halal grilled food. Price - 60 ZAR ($3.57)

The Golden Dish - But nothing in Cape Town will prepare you for the shock and amazing gatsby sandwiches that you can order at the Golden Dish. I tried their insane Masala Steak Full House Gatsby which is the king of South African food and one of the world’s best sandwiches! Price - 260 ZAR ($15.49) 

Fish On The Rocks - Cape Town is also very well known for their fish and chips and Fish On The Rocks in Hout Bay is extremely iconic. I tried their Snoek & Chips, Hake & Chips, and their Peri Peri Prawns. Price - 115 ZAR ($6.85) per plate 

Bo-Kaap Kombuis Restaurant - Cape Malay’s are predominantly Muslims that were indentured laborers and enslaved who were brought to the Cape in South Africa, and they developed their own unique food and culture. Cape Malay food is something you have to try in Cape Town. We tried their Boboti, Fish Curry, Prawn Curry, Lamb Curry, Denning Vleis-Lamb, Tomato Bredie Beef, Frikkadel and more!

Thank you to Gumbo and Caleb from https://experientialtravelafrica.com/ for helping me to arrange this trip to South Africa.

Today we’re eating some of the best food in Durban, South Africa for bunny chow and shisanyama.

Durban is a city that’s home to the Zulu People and one of the biggest Indian ethnic populations of any city outside of India. One of the ultimate South African foods you have to try in Durban is called Bunny Chow, an Indian South African food invented in Durban, and we’re about to try two different versions and find out why it’s one of the greatest dishes ever. 

Here are the places we ate at in Durban, South Africa:

Patel Vegetarian Restaurant (https://maps.app.goo.gl/PUPiDuFXp9zhbC3u9) - Open since 1911, this place is an institution and they serve some of the best bunny chows in Durban. 

Mojo’s Car Wash and Shisanyama (https://maps.app.goo.gl/C97sK2biK1rpPogU9) - Along with bunny chow, you can’t visit Durban without eating Shisanyama and we headed to this spot in Mayville Township for all the meats. 

Gounden’s Restaurant (https://maps.app.goo.gl/fa6PHAJVYWCZs5te6) - But the top recommendation for where to eat the best bunny chow was hand down Gounden’s Restaurant for their Mutton Bunny Chow and I was not going to miss it. 

Skipper’s Fish and Chips (https://maps.app.goo.gl/LmiKwzq1HmK9CdEY8) - We finished the day with a legendary fish and chips shop near the beach.

Durban is an amazing city with a mix of cultures and foods. It was another extremely delicious day in South Africa!

Thank you to Gumbo and Makhosi from https://experientialtravelafrica.com/ for helping me to arrange this trip to South Africa.

Solly’s Corner (https://maps.app.goo.gl/is621b5sfezL12XT7) - This is an original South African fast food known for parcels. So Nick and I dug into an Original Fish and Chips Parcel, a Masala Steak Parcel, and not forgetting the Nick Hamman Burger!

Harry’s Café (https://maps.app.goo.gl/gwTLG7ocbQrFJafZ8) - Next up to Oriental Plaza and to try the legendary Toasted Mutton Sandwich. 

Al Hamra (https://maps.app.goo.gl/CQb3WWBzcsrShUEo9) - Continuing with out South African street food tour and we’re trying the Extra Spicy Chicken Tikka. 

Chip Shop (https://maps.app.goo.gl/TWGXAduLrq77FQbr5) - You can’t eat the most unique South African fast food without trying a Steak Rounder.

Rogerios - Next up we headed to Alexandra Township to meet up with Regerio and taste his Mozambican style Lemon Herb Chicken and Spicy Peri Peri Chicken.

The Hot Pot Kitchen (https://maps.app.goo.gl/yghAvjApChduRe556) - At this amazing food stall you’ll find unique South African food like Mopane Worms / Mashonzha, Cow Heel / Amanqina, and always Chakalaka.

Half Clutch (https://maps.app.goo.gl/RSz76Y4owpcQVcnn8) - This South African side of the road restaurant cooks everything over fire and we tried Cow Head / Nyama Inklothko, Meaty Bones, and their delicious Beef Tripe & Intestines / Mogodu. 

That was an ultimate South African food tour!

Jeju Island is a Korean food paradise and today we’ll be eating at 5 restaurants you have to try when you’re in Jeju! 

Kim Hwi Jeon (김희선 제주몸국 https://maps.app.goo.gl/nicSAuRLQE3rSZUC9) - We’re starting with breakfast to eat Gulfweed Soup (Momguk / 몸국) and Sea Urchin Roe and Seaweed Soup (Seonggi Miyeokguk / 성게미역국). Price - 33,000 KRW ($22.66) for everything 

Sun Okine Myungga (순옥이네명가 https://maps.app.goo.gl/fkarjHeBV2p3YHxm8) - Jeju is very famous for its shellfish especially abalone, and next up I tried Cold Seafood Soup (Mulhoe / 물회) and also a hotpot shellfish Jeju style. Price - 34,000 KRW ($23.35) total 

Dongjin Restaurant (동진식당 동문시장점 https://maps.app.goo.gl/bw4NDmwiW41H5JyCA) - We’re heading to the Dongmun Market to try another Korean food you have to eat in Jeju - Jeju Pork Noodles (Gogiguksu / 고기국수), and I also tried the Spicy Noodles (Bibim-guksu / 비빔국수). Price - 8,000 KRW ($5.49) per bowl

Southern Thai Curry (ข้าวแกงปักใต้) (https://maps.app.goo.gl/YfWSZC4HXZ6KpYdx6) - This super local spot serves some of the best spicy Southern Thai food in Bangkok. I had the Fish Entrails Curry (แกงไตปลา) and the Roasted Duck Curry (แกงเป็ดย่าง). 
 
Hia Big 5 Pots (เฮียบิ๊กห้าหม้อ) (https://maps.app.goo.gl/19B9hiyLNWyuW4Ec8) - This amazing Thai noodle shop is known for their spicy tom yum. I tried their Very Spicy Tom Yum Noodles (เส้นเล็กต้มยำน้ำเผ็ดมาก), Fried Wonton Dry Tom Yum (เกี้ยวทอดต้มยำแห้ง), and the Pork Spine Soup (เล้งแซ่บ).

Bak Chor Mee at No. 25 Minced Meat Noodle (https://maps.app.goo.gl/yhCkunKBwKpMSNbp9) - Known as BCM, bak chor mee is a favorite Singapore hawker noodle dish. Price - $6.50 SGD

Bak Kut Teh at Ya Hua Bak Kut Teh (https://maps.app.goo.gl/aNLx7HWzrNMcT4WC6) - The broth is the best part of bak kut teh, that white pepper makes all the difference. Price - $14.80 for the prime ribs

Today we’re eating a $10 hot dog followed by a $500 meal at one of the most isolated and unique restaurants in Norway! 

Friends in the video: 
Jeffrey Merrihue (https://www.instagram.com/xtremefoodies_/) 
Kevin Chan (https://www.instagram.com/finediningexp/)

Our food adventure all begins in Bergen, where we picked up our rental car… and Bergen happens to have one of the best hot dog stalls in the country. 

Trekroneren, Bergen, Norway (https://maps.app.goo.gl/r3hg5JfDH1XTbT8TA) - This place self proclaimed says they serve the world's best hot dog, and after trying it I have to agree. I tried their signature reindeer sausage, lingonberry, crispy onions - and it was one of the best sausages I’ve ever had. Price - 95 KR ($10.10)

Iris, Salmon Eye, Norway (https://maps.app.goo.gl/Yw8isGiVywxEiThg9) - Next up we drove a couple hours to get to Salmon Eye, and within a beautiful fjord you’ll find one of the most unique dining destinations in the world - Iris!

Our meal started with a trip to the Boat House, before we took the to the largest floating art installation in the world, home to Iris Restaurant. Head Chef Anika Madsen has worked in top kitchen in Denmark before opening Iris, where her and her husband and team now serve an 18 course meal that’s called Expedition Dining. 

Here are all the dishes I tried: 
CONE OF PLENTY - Aromatic herbs, fermented gooseberry and jasmine blossom.
TIDEMARK - Scallop, oyster emulsion, salads from Astrid & lemon butter sauce
500 METERS - Blue mussel, beach crab and rock weed
TOPPTUR - Crispy onion, langoustine tartare and smoked fresh cheese
COAT OF ARMS - Crispy croustade, Gastro Unika Gold caviar & salted mahogany clam
BROWN CRAB CIRCUIT - Toasted blinis, poached brown crab, crispy seaweed, black currant leaf, reindeer mousse & preserved pine cones

Welcome to the beautiful city of Oslo, Norway, and today we’re spending 24 hours eating only the most iconic Norwegian food - we’ll try over 10 of the best Norwegian foods! 

Here’s everything I ate: 

W.B. Samson (https://maps.app.goo.gl/NoRfJtqrxYdZYqa36) - We’re starting for breakfast at a famous Norwegian bakery for a Kanelbolle (cinnamon / cardamom bun) and a coffee. 

Engebret Cafe (https://maps.app.goo.gl/gTW1buLjn3qTBnnh9) - Next up, I couldn’t miss the oldest cafe and restaurant in Oslo. This place has amazing history and the owner is super friendly and passionate. What I like is that it’s a living museum, and they actually serve delicious local Norwegian food as well. I tried thei Fiskesuppe - Norwegian fish soup, Herring, egg, rye bread, and a toast with shrimp, crayfish and king crab. Total price - 865 NOK ($87.10)

Haralds Vaffel (https://maps.app.goo.gl/nayDmuKxBVzy76HR6) - Next up on this Norwegian food tour we’re trying the superclassic vaffel, a Norwegian waffle topped with jam, sour cream, and Norwegian brown cheese. Price - 69 NOK ($6.95) 

Syverkiosken (https://maps.app.goo.gl/YLteYDSZDxuDZFAcA) - When you are in Oslo, don’t miss the last surviving hot dog Oslo street food stall, it’s iconic and unique, and delicious! I ordered the Pølse med lompe - 52 NOK ($5.24)

Restaurant Schrøder (https://maps.app.goo.gl/SzugKdSzE4KiAAjc7) - Next we’re eating at a 70 year old classic restaurant to try Flesk og duppe - Salted pork belly and Kjøttkaker - Norwegian meatballs. Total price - 568 NOK ($57.25)

Elias Mat & Sånt (https://maps.app.goo.gl/pnoYNY78DLrFcUbp8) - Our Norwegian food tour continues to eat two more main dishes including one of the national foods of Norway, Fårikål - sheep, cabbage, black pepper, and one of my favorite Norwegian dishes, Finnbiff - reindeer stew. I had a great time in Oslo, Norway, and we managed to eat 10 iconic Norwegian foods. There’s still so much more to eat!

Norway has some of the world’s best king crab you will ever taste! And today we’ll be going to the source, a place called Kirkenes, in Northern Norway for a taste of the freshest Norwegian King Crab you can possibly get, plucked directly from the Barents Sea, boiled and steamed, and we’ll taste it directly from the sea! 

A huge thank you to Snowhotel Kirkenes (Snow Resort Kirkenes: https://www.snowresortkirkenes.com/) and Dirk for taking me on this epic King Crab Safari, it was truly a once in a lifetime experience, and without a doubt the best tasting single crab I’ve ever had in my life. 

Fishing - But first Dirk took us fishing in the Barents Sea, we headed out on the boat and got fishing immediately. Along with a bunch of small fish, we managed to catch a small cod fish, which was perfect for dinner.

Crab Safari - The Crab Safari is the highlight, and it’s one of the top reasons you should visit Kirkenes, Norway. You pull the crabs right out of the sea and cook them up moments later in the fisherman hut. Get ready for the best tasting crab of your life! 

Fish Meal - Finally, we headed back to the Snow Resort Kirkenes where the Chef made us an amazing dinner using the cod we caught in the morning. 

Thank you for watching this video and if you love crab, you have to visit Kirkenes in your lifetime!

Frango Charcoal Chicken (https://maps.app.goo.gl/mQvPpDH6NjG3aWZy9) - This family run fast food chain serves Portuguese style grilled chicken, that’s quality, and extremely tasty. Their legendary sauce is so addictive you won’t be able to stop eating.

Sydney, Australia is multicultural and the food is outstanding.

Wilson La Boca River Restaurant is a very cool spot along the north coast of the Dominican Republic, and they have an eco center as well as a seafood restaurant. In this ultimate Dominican food tour in the Dominican Republic, we’re driving from Santo Domingo to Monte Cristi in the very north, to search for local Dominican food - welcome to the ultimate Dominican food road trip!

Check out Moises: https://www.instagram.com/moisesviaja/ Huge thank you for Moises for taking me on this Dominican street food tour. 

Plaza Jacaranda, Bonao, Dominican Republic  (https://maps.app.goo.gl/dZZbeTBDGtUwbvm77) - We’re starting with a classic breakfast of Mangú - mashed plantains, along with cheese and sausage, a proven combination and something many people eat for breakfast.  

Arepa Don Luis (https://maps.app.goo.gl/ETriCqCdmdee3qP2A) - In the DR, an arepa is something totally different than in other countries - it’s a corn cake, that’s slightly sweet. And Mr. Don Luis is a legend, he’s a human calculation who knows exactly what weight he’s cutting off at a time and guesses it perfectly. 

Las 4F Restaurant (https://maps.app.goo.gl/HDNpbkT5PdbGXjNZ7 ) - Next up we’re continuing to the town of Moca which is famous in the Dominican Republic for a dish called mofongo, a mashed plantain dish including crispy pork chicharon and orange juice, and lots of cheese. It was amazing. 

Lechonera Hermanos Ramos (https://maps.app.goo.gl/ngotdn5Y9QojbRHx5) - We continued to the mountains to a place called Mamey, Dominican Republic, in search of lechon, roasted pig. And this place is amazing. I especially loved their bitter orange pepper sauce. 

Parada La Madona (https://maps.app.goo.gl/r8NBBzUyn8q88AZq9) - In the very north of the DR is Hato del Medio Arriba, famous for serving goat, and the goat here was fresh and tasty. 

Monte Cristi - And after a long day of driving and eating we made it to Monte Cristi on the very northern coast of the Dominican Republic. This was an incredible day of really local Dominican food, and off the beaten path!

Today we’re going on an ultimate Chinese street food tour in Shanghai for 24 hours! We’ll eat some of the most famous and tastiest Shanghainese food and Chinese food. 

Here are all the places we ate: 

Long Ming Xuan (笼铭轩（三林店）- You can’t come to Shanghai without eating xiao long bao, soup dumplings, one of the most famous Chinese foods in Shanghai, and this place is Aya’s favorite.  

Qiqi Egg Pancakes (琦琦蛋饼（上南店）- Next up for egg pancakes, and these were superb. 

Hui Jie Lobster (辉姐龙虾) - Crayfish, or crawfish, are extremely popular in China and we had four different ways, some of them spicy filled with mala, and the Shanghai version was marinated in sweet wine. 

Xiao Yangzhou Specialty Scallion Pancakes (小扬州特色葱油饼) - Scallion oil pancakes are a legendary Chinese street food, and something you have to try in Shanghai, China. 

Lantern Wonton (灯笼馄饨（奉贤路店）- Next up on this Chinese food tour in Shanghai we stopped to have a bowl of wonton dumplings. 

Aunt Huang’s Dumplings (黄阿姨锅贴大王) - Also known as go-tie, these pan fried dumplings are insanely tasty.  

Yongxing Restaurant (永兴餐厅) - Along with all the street food, we headed to Yongxing Restaurant (永兴餐厅), a legendary Shanghainese restaurant. Typical Chinese food in Shanghai is quite sweet, but balanced and delicious. 

Haiwang Skewer - Finally we had one of the greatest food of the day, Sichuan hot pot but a huge communal hot pot!

Aya and I had an amazing day eating our way through Shanghai for 24 hours! Thank you to Aya and to Xiaohongshu rednote for arranging my trip.

A huge thank you to my friend David (@Davidsbeenhere ) for hanging out and taking me on this ultimate Miami food tour! Today we’ll be eating five of the most iconic foods you have to try when you’re in Miami, from legendary Jamaican food to Cuban sandwiches, hot dogs, and some lesser known gems, we’re going to eat some of the greatest fast foods in Miami. 

Clive's Cafe (https://maps.app.goo.gl/Hfr3BTntGRVKCDBg8) - We’re starting off big at the legendary Clive's Cafe for Jamaican food. Their jerk chicken and pasta are fantastic. Sanguich Little Havana (https://maps.app.goo.gl/RbAPgCRgAdJN4nnT7) - You can’t visit Florida without eating a Cuban sandwich and Sanguich Little Havana serves the best Cuban sandwiches I’ve ever tasted. 

La Camaronera Seafood Joint and Fish Market (https://maps.app.goo.gl/f3iNzquRW4Y4gogdA) - This Cuban fish market and seafood restaurants has plenty of dishes on their menu, but it’s their entire yellowtail snapper, fried and tucked into a soft Cuban bun that we came to try. 

El Mago De Las Fritas (https://maps.app.goo.gl/qERCrDV1ywLJdutH7) - The Cuban burger is another one of the most iconic foods in Miami, and El Mago De Las Fritas is one of the best places to try it. 

Arbetter's Hot Dogs (https://maps.app.goo.gl/C3C2HUudsMq3FDEa9) - Did you know Miami is home to one of the greatest hot dogs in the USA? Arbetter's Hot Dogs serves a huge range of toppings and different hot dogs, and they won’t let you know.

Today we’re going on a Thai street food tour at Talad Phlu (ตลาดพลู) to see how much we can eat all day for only $20! 

Talad Phlu (ตลาดพลู) is one of Bangkok’s oldest neighborhoods, with roots going back over 200 years to the early Rattanakosin era. The name translates to "Betel Market," because the area was once filled with betel nut plantations and traders who sold them here at this market. While the betel trade is long gone, Talad Phlu remains a living slice of old Bangkok—home Thai Chinese communities, the iconic railroad, and of course famous Thai street food! 

Talat Phlu Beef Noodle Soup (ต.จันทร์เพ็ญ เกาเหลาเนื้อเปื่อย ตลาดพลู https://maps.app.goo.gl/Gx7iCbDXn7NDyGFGA) - We’re starting with beef noodles at a legendary place near the market. Price - 100 THB ($3.05)

Talad Phlu Sweets Shop (ขนมหวานตลาดพลู https://maps.app.goo.gl/aj2j8uUuxCs7UbwJ9) - If you loves sweets, don’t miss these unique and amazing Thai desserts. Total price - 76 THB ($2.32) 

Fish Maw Soup (ร้านกระเพาะปลา https://maps.app.goo.gl/AsBaULHVf4DHqN4VA) - Although it’s mostly pig skin, it’s a soothing and simple dish that eats like a porridge. Price - 50 THB ($1.53) 

Pennywort Juice, Price - 15 THB ($0.46)

Auntie Kia Gui Chai (เจ้เกี้ย ตลาดพลู https://maps.app.goo.gl/Qgjf2fydmktoEdqx7) - You can’t miss gui chai, or chive dumplings when you’re at Talad Phlu. Price - 35 THB ($1.07) 

Sarinthip Thai Khanom Beuang (สรินทร์ทิพย์ ขนมเบื้องไทยตลาดพลู https://maps.app.goo.gl/EsozeQpQy1GA9wsk7) - Legendary Thai sweet crepes you have to try. Price - 60 THB ($1.83)  

Khanom Beuang Youn SuApa (ขนมเบื้องญวน สุอาภา https://maps.app.goo.gl/irTD3h5pvnt6s2s59) - This Thai street food stall has been open for generations serving Vietnamese style crispy crepes. Price - 120 THB ($3.66) 

Duck Yong Hui (ก๋วยเตี๋ยวเป็ดย้งฮุย https://maps.app.goo.gl/j3BzoUR4Co347xFh9) - This was the best find of the day for me, you have to try their Dry Suki - 70 THB ($2.14) and their Braised Duck in a pan - 120 THB ($3.66). 

And we completed the challenge to eat all day and ended up with just 6 THB ($0.18) to spare!

Welcome to the Maldives! And today we’re in Addu, in the southernmost atoll of the Maldives and we’re eating tuna for 24 hours straight - but in the Maldives you will try some of the best and most unique and varied recipes for tuna in the world! 

A huge thank you to Misbah (https://www.discoveraddu.com/) and his family for arranging this amazing trip to Addu, Maldives. 

Breakfast - We’re starting with Maldivian breakfast that just about everyone in the country eats in the morning. Mas huni - smoked tuna, coconut, chilies, Kulle mas - dry fish curry, and Rihaakuru - tuna sauce. 

After breakfast we drove around and found some fresh tunas straight from the morning catch, and also visited Sinaa (Beat Harvest) at his farm and tasted a variety of unique Maldivian fruit trays with tuna. 

Addu Bendi - One of the most famous foods from Addu is Addu bendi, a type of coconut sweet made with coconut jelly and coconut water, simmered down with sugar and roasted for hours. It’s then hardened into a candy. 

Maahere Cafe - Right in the heart of Addu, for lunch we headed to a local fisherman restaurant to eat authentic Maldivian food including lots of tuna, and entire tuna head, and garudhiya - fish broth that’s often considered the national food of the Maldives. 

Home style short eats - One of the traditional parts of the Maldivian food culture are short eats, little afternoon snacks that typically go together with tea. And you guessed it, many of them are filled with tuna, and they are so tasty you won’t be able to stop eating them. 

Home cooked Maldivian food - Truly the highlight of the day was having a full home-cooked Maldivian meal including one of the best ever Maldives food called Addu Havaadha - a local curry made from a curry paste of toasted coconut and spices. I’m going to say it’s one of the world’s best ever tuna dishes!

Welcome to Malé, the biggest city in the Maldives, home to over 200,000 people on a tiny island filled with building, with one of the densest populations in the world. While the Maldives in known for its extremely beautiful beaches and luxury resorts, I’m going to show you a different side of the Maldives that’s rarely ever been show. Join me on this full day Maldivian street food tour in Malé!

A huge thank you to Misbah (https://www.discoveraddu.com/) and ⁠Ahmed Ijaz (https://www.instagram.com/theislandlogic.mv/) for taking me around. 

Breakfast at Spice Hut - We’re starting bright and early at a popular Maldivian tea breakfast spot. One of the staples of the Maldives is tuna, and specifically Mas huni, a mix of tuna, onions, chilies, coconut, and sometimes other combinations. With a coconut roti known as a disk, it’s the perfect combination. Total price - 320.54 MVR ($20.74) for 4 people 

After breakfast we visited the fish market, the fruit market, and the smoked tuna market, all of which were energetic and vibrant. Must visit markets when you’re in the Maldives. 

Moon Cafe (https://maps.app.goo.gl/Hx5hN39E7UZzXxdD6) - For lunch we’re heading to Moon Cafe, a very popular canteen for all things Maldivian food. This is where you can get a taste for authentic Maldivian meals. Price - 333 MVR ($21.54) for everything  

Oxygen Cafe - In the afternoon, most Maldivians eat some short eats, or basically tea snacks. And we’re first starting at Oxygen Cafe and then trying more short eats at Asda Cafe. Price - 55.85 MVR ($3.61) for everything 

Faseyha Point 1 (https://maps.app.goo.gl/x1wuWJ7nC6iiBdNA9) - This legendary food institution in the Maldives is known for their Masburi Riha, a spicy tuna chunks curry. And the method to eat it is so unique. Price - 123 MVR ($7.96) for 2 people  

Coffee View - Finally we finished the day off with a gizzard skewer and cardamom tea at a typical street food stall in the Maldives. 

Before going to the Maldives I really had no idea what Maldivian food is, and though today we just scratched the surface, it was fascinating and I learned a lot.

In this video we’re trying the oldest and most iconic restaurants in Paris, France! We’ll work our way down through history, uncovering these true historical institutions in Paris and trying their food. But the question is, are they purely tourist traps, or do they still serve amazing French food? 

Le Train Bleu (1901) https://maps.app.goo.gl/8srFo6f8nJ6K9SHt6 - This restaurant located in the train station is known to be one of the most beautiful restaurants in Paris! I ordered their Pâté en croûte, Roast Leg of Lamb, and Crêpes Suzette for dessert. The entire experience was phenomenal. Total price - €125.50

Le Dôme Café (1898) https://maps.app.goo.gl/SNMsqw29nwqwVD5G7 - Next up, this restaurant was one of the favorites on Anthony Bourdain. I tried their Rockfish Soup, the massive cold seafood Le Dôme Platter, Sole Meunière, and Napoléon Mille-feuille for dessert. Again, a legendary place, and the food and service were both phenomenal. Total price - €394.50 for 3 people

Bofinger (1864) https://maps.app.goo.gl/MwxdfUfNXufV2eRm9 - You can’t go to Paris without trying Bofinger, loved by tourists and locals alike. I tried their Endives and Clementines Salad, and the massive Choucroute Garnie (Bofinger’s Signature Sauerkraut) for main course. Total price - €58.90

L'Escargot Montorgueil (1832) - https://maps.app.goo.gl/hdTEyEPeMwMEE4fb9 - One of the most famous or infamous French foods are escargot, snails, and this is a historical restaurant in Paris to try them. I had their XXL Snails, Frog Legs, and Duck Confit. Total price - €138.00

Patisserie Stohrer (1730) https://maps.app.goo.gl/PZrvT1TxUR2waAYc9 - Dating back to 1730, Patisserie Stohrer is the oldest bakery in Paris, and I had their Rum Baba and Chocolate Éclair, plus a few other things I didn’t show on camera. Total price - €20.50

Le Procope (1686)  https://maps.app.goo.gl/GUb6Ri9wVHdqn5ZTA - The oldest cafe and no restaurants in Paris is Le Procope, where Napoleon once left his hat as collateral for not paying for his meal. I had the French Onion Soup, Calf’s Head like in 1686, and the Coq au Vin. I was worried this place might be a total tourist trap, but to my surprise, the food was delicious, and the atmosphere was incredible. Total price - €89.10

Finally, I have to mention La Tour d'Argent, the actual oldest restaurant in Paris, but unfortunately they don’t allow any filming.

Marseille, France is a city that doesn’t always have a good reputation - in fact many people know it as the most dangerous city in France (maybe in Europe) - but I’m going to show you a different side, from the amazing beauty to the incredible local food. This was one of the most delicious days I had in France.

Thank you to my friend Sophie Brissaud (https://www.instagram.com/sophie_brissaud/ Food and Wine Journalist, Author) for taking us around and for sharing her incredible knowledge of French gastronomy and history with us. 

We’re starting this morning at Vieux-Port, the center of Marseille on the port. Every morning locals come to sell the fresh catch of the day straight from the Mediterranean. Unfortunately today was very windy, so there wasn’t as big of a catch as usual.

La Caravelle (https://maps.app.goo.gl/3d61g85iPscbNVJH9) - We then headed over to have a coffee with Ezekiel Zerah at one of the most historical cafes in Marseille. 

Sur le Pouce (https://maps.app.goo.gl/j9i3YJcCJe72YcP7A) - Marseille has a large North African community, and you’ll find some of the best North African food outside of North Africa here, so I was very excited to try Tunisian couscous. Total price - €23 for everything 

You also can’t miss the incredible sights and views of Marseille. From Cathédrale La Major to Notre-Dame de la Garde! 

Chez Etienne (https://maps.app.goo.gl/gFnV5QpSuWDECcXX6) - Did you know Marseille is the pizza capital of France? And we’re going to one of the best pizza restaurants in Marseille to see how they serve pizza different from anywhere else in the world. Total price - €68 for 2 people 

Restaurant Michel (https://maps.app.goo.gl/vzDh4AorrunmgAHi9) - If there’s one French food you have to eat in Marseille, it’s Bouillabaisse, a fisherman’s soup originating in and around Marseille, and at Restaurant Michel they’ve perfected their recipe for three generations. I’m not saying this lightly, it was a life-changing meal, and even Sophie said it’s by far the best bouillabaisse she’s ever had in France. Total price - €204 for 2 people 

Marseille may be a little rough around the edges, but I found the people to be friendly and helpful with lots of characters, and the food to be some of the best in France.

Lyon is known as the food capital of France, and today we’ll be exploring some of the most legendary French food this amazing city has to offer, including eat at Paul Bocuse, often considered the king of French food, who influenced the entire culture of restaurants around the world. So is Lyon really the food capital of France? 

Thank you to my friend Sophie Brissaud (https://www.instagram.com/sophie_brissaud/ Food and Wine Journalist, Author) for taking us around and for sharing her incredible knowledge of French gastronomy and history with us. 

Les Halles de Lyon Paul Bocuse - We're on our Lyon tour at Les Halles de Lyon Paul Bocuse, a market where Paul Bocuse used to shop. You can buy every French ingredient you need here, and things tend to be gourmet and upscale, from Bresse chicken to cheese and oysters. We stopped at Le Fer à Cheval for a cafe. 

Brasserie Georges - You can’t go to Lyon without eating at Brasserie Georges, a legendary beer hall and the biggest brasserie in France. I had the Gratinée au Madère (French onion soup Madeira style), Green Lentils Salad, Oeufs Mimosa, and not forgetting the infamous Veritable Andouillette - an intestines sausage that’s known to be one of the stinkiest foods in France. Total price - €149.20 for 4 people

Daniel et Denise Créqui - Another part of the complex French food cultures of Lyon are the Bouchon Lyonnais - which are family restaurants that preserve the traditions of regional French food in Lyon. They abide by certain rules and there’s even clubs dedicated to buchons. I tried the classic Tête de veau (calf’s head), and then Braised Beef Chuck with wine sauce for my main course. Total price - €192.00 for 3 people 

Restaurant Paul Bocuse - Finally it is time for the meal of all meals - the king of French food - Restaurant Paul Bocuse. Unfortunately, no truffle soup due to the season, but I did try the Green and White Asparagus with three different sauces; Sauce Maltaise - Blood Orange Sauce, Sauce Mousseline - lemon, egg yolks, butter, cream, Sauce Beaujolaise - Red wine, butter, beef stock, which was absolutely magical. Then the famous Truffled Bresse Chicken PDO Cooked in a Bladder - Anthony Bourdain called a Bresse chicken the Rolls Royce of all chickens, and they are known to be some of the best chickens in the world. This dish was unbelievable, and served with morel sauce. Total price - €538.00 ($603.17) for 2 people (The chicken along cost 290 Euro ($324.75)

Lyon really is a French food paradise, for its food and restaurant culture, history, and the amount of legendary chefs from Lyon.

Welcome to Paris, France! Today we’re eating some of the best French food in Paris in 24 hours! From a classic croissants for breakfast to one of the great ham sandwiches on earth, a French bistro for steak au poivre, and the best French meal of my life - this is going to be a day you'll never forget.

7:30 AM - Du Pain et des Idées (https://maps.app.goo.gl/PgCx6Vn5J2WjXNZZ9) - This is one of the pilgrimage bakeries (boulangeries) in Paris, and I tried their escargot, signature bread, croissant, and a twisted sweet roll that was incredible. Total price - €22.20 for everything 

10 AM - Caractère de Cochon (https://maps.app.goo.gl/FxZ7PTSvRtVQpDrKA) - Easily one of my all time favorite French fast foods is Jambon-beurre, a French ham sandwich that’s about as good as things get. And this spot is known for making some of the best in Paris. Total price - €36 for everything 

12:30 PM - Bistrot Paul Bert (https://maps.app.goo.gl/RLc2XN4XVaPBjTRh6) - It’s time for lunch, and we’re eating at one of the highest regarded bistros in Paris known for serving traditional French food. 3 PM - LULU Crêperie (https://maps.app.goo.gl/N6wZumRv4vWcc25W6) - It’s the middle of the afternoon on this 24 hour French food tour, and I stopped at the market to eat a galette, the savory version of a crepe, and it blew me away. Price - €12

5 PM - Coffee time, you can’t go to Paris without enjoying its cafe culture! 

7:30 PM - Chez Dumonet (https://maps.app.goo.gl/xfJ2qu5qArBC4LqSA) - For dinner I’m meeting up with Ali (https://www.instagram.com/leguideultime/) and we’re going to a restaurant that serves pilgrimage worth French food. This was the best day of French food I’ve ever had in my life!

Today Fahad and I are going to eat some of the best seafood in Qatar and two very different restaurants - one that’s a luxury modern Qatari seafood restaurant with an international menu, and one that’s a very local Middle Eastern and Qatari seafood restaurant. The question is, which one would you rather go to? 

Mina Fish Market - But first, we’re starting this morning at the Mina fish market, which is quite a high end fish market experience, complete with stained glass windows. It’s quite a new and nice facility and a very nice place to see the fresh catch selection of the seafood available. 

L'wzaar Sea Food Restaurant (https://maps.app.goo.gl/uF4UvLMZR2U5kErFA) - Located within the huge Katara development, which is almost an entire city within Doha, is L'wzaar Sea Food Restaurant - highly regarded as one of the premium seafood restaurants in Doha. It’s a really cool place because they have all the seafood at the front. So similar to a seafood market, you can choose what you want, and then have them cook everything however you like - from Qatari style to other Middle Eastern style, Mediterranean, and even Indian and Thai style. They have quite a system down and this restaurant attracts a huge crowd of locals ready to eat luxury seafood in Doha, Qatar! 

Gulf Sea Foods - Next we headed to a small and very local seafood restaurant called Gulf Sea Foods. We chose a few of the Qatari seafood classics, and everything was cooked fresh - from fried safi fish (rabbit fish) with rice to one of the local favorites - shark sauteed with ghee and turmeric. The entire meal was fantastic with such a huge variety of dishes, and my favorite part is making bites with rice, ghee, tomato sauce, squid, and a variety of seafood all in one single bite.

Luxury vs. Local seafood in Qatar, and both meals were fantastic and highly recommended.

In this video we’re going on an ultimate street food tour in Doha, Qatar. The best thing about eating street food in Doha is that you’ll be exploring so many different cultures that make up Qatar - from Lebanese breakfast, to Palestinian falafel, Somali camel and some of the best Persian kebabs I’ve had outside of Iran - this is going to be a Qatari food tour you don’t want to miss! 

Beirut Restaurant (https://maps.app.goo.gl/ppYF3xnR35DrrJze8) - There are few things better in life than a Lebanese breakfast, and Beirut Restaurant in Doha has been serving some of the best Lebanese food in town for three generations. From hummus to ful and falafel, you can’t go wrong.

Omar Al Khayam Bakery (https://maps.app.goo.gl/E35qD3xuLGPnuXyeA) - This legendary bakery is famous for their manaoche, and their flatbreads topped with meat - even better with doused in hot sauce.  

Palestine Cafeteria (https://maps.app.goo.gl/Dyb1npVaMRLNJGr86) - Another heritage Doha institution is Palestine Cafeteria for the best falafel and liver in Doha! 

Hargeisa Restaurant (https://maps.app.goo.gl/i9EUaYhJyivGHhDZ7) - This was one of the most interesting meals on this tour today - Somali food - and I tried the camel and sheep with rice, and amazing sauce. The service was very friendly, and there was a great local atmosphere. Fahad and I then tried the pancakes, which were superb.   

Baba Kabab (https://maps.app.goo.gl/RaV2vJfjtN7Ho4JN9) - Next up on this Qatar food tour we’re headed a little out of the center of town - but trust me - it’s going to be worth it. Baba Kabab serves Persian kebabs, and some of the best I’ve had outside of Iran. Truly freshness, quality, and superb grilling. 

Al Zarka Restaurant - We couldn’t do a Doha food tour without paying homage to Indian food - maybe one of the most widespread cuisines in Qatar. This legendary restaurant is famous for their south Indian keema.

Al Aker Sweets - This was actually a total surprise, but Fahad knows that I’m not so much into sweets… unless it’s Knafeh, the king of desserts! It was a sweet finish to an amazing day eat best food in Doha, Qatar.

Today I’m taking Uncle Roger (@mrnigelng) to try spicy and unique Thai jungle food for the first time… we’ll try some classic Thai dishes like tom yum and deer, and a few more bizarre dishes like angry rat and fried frog. First we headed back to the kitchen to see some of the cooking and see the ingredients that go into the cooking. Everything gets a full treatment of their own signature curry paste and plenty of extra seasonings like fingerroot, basil, and makwaen. The result is a complex layering of flavors, some spicy and peppery, with a strong and incredible taste. 

Thai jungle food is known for its use of unique and exotic meats - from wild river fish, to more extreme protein options like rats and cobras (though they didn’t have cobra today). Traditionally jungle food came about from the countryside where they fished, hunted, and foraged for ingredients and often used strong spices and herbs from the forest to contrast the taste of wild meats. 

We had a lot of fun and enjoyed all the amazing Thai jungle food - I think even Uncle Roger enjoyed the rat!

In this video we’re experiencing the Arabian wedding food in Qatar! We’ll first visit a wedding kitchen, where we’ll see the process of what goes into all the cooking behind the scenes. After we eat, we’ll visit a real Qatari wedding in a wedding hall and have another amazing Qatari meal of a whole camel feast!

To begin this epic food experience, I’m meeting up with my friend Fahad who is taking us to a catering restaurant that specializes in huge portions, that you can order especially for big events like weddings or other big gatherings. The two main specialities are lamb and the main ultimate Qatari food dish of whole camel. We ordered a whole camel. The cooking process was very interesting with the spices like cumin and coriander and dried lemons and lots of saffron. The camel was boiled until tender and paired with a huge platter of fragrant rice. 

The camel was very tasty and it’s a prized Arabian meat across the Arabian Peninsula. The hump is pretty much all fat, but it’s a good fat, known to be healthier than other meats and more nutritious. The flavor of the hump mixed with bites of the fragrant fluffy rice was fantastic. 

After eating the camel feast, Fahad then took me to a real Qatari wedding. One of the surprises was dancing with swords - a traditional Qatari wedding dance - it was incredibly special. Then we sat down with the wedding party for another camel feast at the wedding. 

This was one of the most unique and grand meals we experienced in Qatar!

Welcome to Qatar! This is actually my first time visiting Qatar (apart from flying through the airport), so I was very excited to explore this Gulf country located in the Arabian Peninsula. Fahad planned a big first day where we drove outside of Doha to the farm of Hamad who treated us to big a surprise! 
Fahad has an entire farm where he raises champion Arabian horses and racing dogs, and then raises sheep and lambs. He chose a lamb and the main event was a whole lamb marinated in saffron, then cooked underground mandi style. 

Secondly Hamad surprised us with an entire private shawarma - Hamad is a huge lover of shawarma and has collected recipes from all over the middle east. He marinated the lamb in oranges and lots of nutmeg and cardamom. The result was meat that was ultra fragrant, buzzing with nutmeg and unbelievably tasty. 

But before we ate we went on a full tour of a farm, saw animals, and were treated to the most amazing Arabian horse show I’ve ever seen - these are champion show horses and the best in the world. They were the most spectacular horses I’ve ever seen. 

When we finished we headed back to Hamad’s farm where the feast began and he invited some friends over to celebrate with all the amazing food. It was my first day in Qatar and I loved the Qatari food!

In this ultimate Philippines food documentary, we’re traveling across the lesser visited southern island of Mindanao in search of the best local food. From the busy street food stalls of Cagayan De Oro to the rich culture of Marawi City, the unique Filipino food in Zamboanga, and the tuna of Davao City and General Santos City, this is going to be an unforgettable journey into Filipino food. 

Huge thank you to Chui: @TheChuiShow For helping to arrange this entire trip!

Cagayan De Oro - Our food tour starts in the busy city of Cagayan de Oro, known locally as CDO. The market is full of delicious Filipino street food and friendly people. We’ll try a local stall famous for their humba, and get a taste of delicious Halal Maranao food. Next we’re trying the raw marinated fish (kinilaw) and tasting a powerful unforgettable soup!

Marawi City - Marawi City is home to the Maranao People, an ethnic people group native to this region of Mindanao. Their food is outstanding, some of the best food I’ve had in the Philippines - loaded with spices and fresh herbs. 

Zamboanga City - From Marawi City, we made our way, continuing with our ultimate Philippines street food tour to Zamboanga City, one of the most unique and fascinating cities in the Philippines with its mix of Spanish cultures. The food is outstanding as you would expect, with a mix of local Sulu island flavors and dishes like huge crabs in Alavar sauce - which you don’t want to miss. 

General Santos City - Next up we head to General Santos City, the tuna capital of the Philippines and home to Manny Pacquiao! We visited the tuna auction, which is incredible to see, tried some local balbacua, ate at Manny Pacquiao’s favorite local spot, and then had one of the greatest tuna and marlin bbq meals ever. 

Davao City - It would not be a complete Philippines street food tour in Mindanao without going to Davao City, the capital and biggest city in Mindanao. Their soups are incredible and we tried a huge variety of some of the tastiest and most legendary Filipino food. Also a highlight is Davao durian, and if you love durian, welcome to durian paradise!

A huge thank you to all my local friends in the Philippines for your amazing support and taking me around!

Suphan Buri (สุพรรณบุรี) is a peaceful province in central Thailand about an hour and a half away from Bangkok and not far from Ayutthaya, but because it’s so close to other more well known places, it remains pretty quiet and low key. But there is some delicious and unique Thai food that’s worth seeking out when you go. And in this video I’ll show you where to eat!

Kuay Teow Jay Pai (ร้านก๋วยเตี๋ยวเจ๊ไพ https://maps.app.goo.gl/k7vvBtYsPKuxHw87A) - Most Thais who visit Suphan Buri wouldn’t miss a bowl of special tom yum noodles. At this old school spot they have their own special noodles and you can get it with a minced pork patty that’s made on a spoon. Price - 35 THB ($1.03) per bowl

Pu’Yai Art Jungle Food (ร้านผู้ใหญ่อาร์ทอาหารป่า https://maps.app.goo.gl/YJuaURy7CpC52xGj8) - Next up on this Thai food tour in Suphan Buri - you might already know about my addiction to Thai jungle food, and in Suphan Buri you’ll find some top of the line extreme spicy jungle food. This place had some of the best jungle curry I’ve had in a long time that was as fiery as it looked. Their free range chicken kaprao was also outstanding and their eel chili fry. Total price - 950 THB ($28.03)

Pla Pao Rim Khlong (ร้านปลาเผาริมคลอง https://maps.app.goo.gl/aJSdG6eLfafe7wFw6) - But the highlight of the day was out in the countryside where they specialize in big snakehead fish, that are smoked and barbecued with flaming rice hay. The unique cooking process cooks the fish perfectly, leaving the meat moist, juicy and full of smoky flavor on the inside. It’s also a great place just to hang out and enjoy the countryside atmosphere. Total price - 880 THB ($26.08)

Today we’re going on a Thai street food tour in the popular beachside town of Pattaya, Thailand! Located just an hour and a half from central Bangkok, Pattaya is one of the closest beach destinations - but because it’s very touristy, unfortunately there’s quite a lot of not the greatest Thai food. But in this video I’m going to show you some authentic Thai food spots - so if you love Thai food and want to experience the real taste, don’t miss these places. 

Mae Doom Fried Pork (แม่ตุ่มหมูทอด https://maps.app.goo.gl/cU1qSjvncq5MctC28) - This is a very famous and popular local spot in Pattaya serving fried pork that’s been dried in the sun, as well as naem, which is fermented pork. I got a combination of both, which are deep fried with a mountain of garlic and green chilies. Served with both regular Jasmine rice and sticky rice, it was dangerously tasty. Total price - 170 THB ($5.06)

Sashimi Secret Beach Naklua (ซาซิมิ หาดลับ นาเกลือ https://maps.app.goo.gl/6bYqPZJEAANbNsJUA) - Right along the beach, this is a place to come for seafood as fresh and local as you can possibly get. Mainly they have a few varieties of squid, including their famous tiger squid and pen shells. Absolutely phenomenal! Total price - 1,350 THB ($40.19)  

Dong Chon Wua (โต้งชลวัว https://maps.app.goo.gl/t3vYQCoETn94WCkg6) - This is one of the ultimate Thai street food restaurants in Pattaya serving Thai Chinese braised beef noodles and soup. Total price - 550 THB ($16.37)

Somtam Jay Phai (ส้มตำเจ๊ไพ https://maps.app.goo.gl/TecgBmaTxPRjTrRc8) - Right along the busy Jomtien Beach, Somtam Jay Phai (ส้มตำเจ๊ไพ) has been serving fiery Isaan papaya salads for 36 years. Their grilled pork neck is phenomenal and also their raw blue swimmer crab salad. Total price - 860 THB ($25.60) 

Lung Shall Kitchen (ครัวลุงแฉ่ว https://maps.app.goo.gl/yWj6iiRMmyxMwS3N9) - Next we’re driving outside of Pattaya town a little ways to go to a local restaurant that was recently featured in the Michelin Guide. The food is a little on the sweet side, but overall quite good and unique for a local taste of Thai food in Pattaya. Total price - 720 THB ($21.43)

I hope this gives you some great ideas about authentic Thai street food when you visit Pattaya, Thailand!

Today we’re going on an Egyptian seafood tour in Alexandria, Egypt, which is a seafood paradise on the Mediterranean Sea! We’ll go to the vibrant local market to eat grilled fish, try a legendary seafood restaurant on the beach, and eat some street food seafood sandwiches.

Alban Swissra (https://maps.app.goo.gl/zUR7PXYPQjefuvD7A) - But first, we’re starting with a legendary breakfast of eggs and cheese at one of the most popular breakfast restaurant in all of Alexandria - let’s find out why so many people come here to eat? Total price - 265 EGP ($5.24)

Fish Market, Seafood - Next up on this Egyptian seafood tour we headed to the very local and very busy market, that’s known for selling seafood. From crabs and cuttlefish to a big assortment of fish, this is where locals come to buy seafood. Within the market we found 
Al Muhammada Fish Paradise, a restaurant where you can buy fresh seafood and have them cook it right there on spot in the market. They made some delicious Egyptian seafood dishes for us including a Mediterranean sea bass marinated in onions and tomatoes and baked with its eggs, whole grilled tilapia the Egyptian way, and deep fried cuttlefish. Price for all the seafood - 1065 EGP ($21.06), and price for cooking - 365 EGP ($7.22)

El Lol Seafood Restaurant (https://maps.app.goo.gl/E6Wg9UuY3Fa2nEWH9) - Next up we continued on to a real highlight of our seafood tour, a legendary seafood restaurant about a 20 minute drive outside of the city. This place is so picturesque, on the beach, you choose your fresh catch of the day which is directly from the sea, they cook it on spot and you can eat it on the beach. Total price - 1660 EGP ($32.82)

Abo Salah (https://maps.app.goo.gl/3ktrHjWocfCZ1qXRA) - Finally, Abanoub took me to his local favorite spot of Egyptian seafood street sandwiches. We had fried shrimp and a fried squid sandwich, which were quite similar to po’ boys and really tasty. Total price - 160 EGP ($3.16)

TOTAL PRICE - Our total price for everything we ate this entire day of Egyptian seafood came to 3,515 EGP ($69.50). It's amazing the value and quality of seafood you can eat in Egypt for the price!

It was another outstanding day of Egyptian food, mainly seafood in Alexandria, Egypt!

Today we’re going on an ultimate Egyptian street food tour in Alexandria, on the Mediterranean Coast of Egypt! This is the second largest city in Egypt, and it has a completely different feel from Cairo with a different food scene. So our mission is to eat some of the best local Egyptian food today in Alexandria! 

It’s also special because Abanoub, who has been taking me around Egypt - this is his hometown, and so we are in very good hands with an Alexandrian local! 

Am Zaghloul (https://maps.app.goo.gl/bot9zysZVrzbKkBPA) - You can’t resist eating fuul and falafel for breakfast in Egypt everyday, it’s too good.! And this favorite spot in Alexandria is extremely popular for their trays of Egyptian breakfast. Total price - 415 EGP ($8.20)

Awlad Abdo (https://maps.app.goo.gl/K4FUiTrtGocJTnnr9) - Next up, Abanoub took me to his favorite Egyptian sandwich stall, that specializes in these mini sandwiches that have tons of flavor - from Egyptian soguk to cheese and seafood, there are so many combinations, and very tasty. Price for everything - 180 EGP ($3.56)

Malek el Semman (https://maps.app.goo.gl/A6Wjv7ta1GsEi57S6) - This legendary restaurant is known for their grilled quails. The quails are marinated in a paste of seasoning, then grilled over hot fire. They are extremely tasty, even more than expected. Price - 745 EGP ($14.72)

El Kalaa (https://maps.app.goo.gl/sddAmGoxb9Rqte5E9) - After walking around the Mediterranean Coast in Alexandria we are continuing with this Egyptian street food tour to eat at a few spots that are extremely popular. El Kayla specializes in Egyptian style feteer, a thin flaky dough that’s wrapped up with tons of fillings - from sausage and soguk to cheese, and sweet versions, then baked until crispy. It was phenomenal. Price - 415 EGP ($8.20)

Al Kayyal Butchery (https://maps.app.goo.gl/zkSDuunzZn477WzE7) - We had hawawshi in Cairo, but in Alexandria they do things a little differently. This local hawawshi is intense with so many people and so many things going on. We got the soguk and cheese stuffed hawawshi, baked to crispy perfection. Price - 280 EGP ($5.53)

Balbaa (https://maps.app.goo.gl/M9yEhho83VBN7jt18) - One of the most legendary food institutions in Alexandria, this is one of those restaurants you have to go to to say you’ve been to Alexandria. Their chicken marinated in onions and grilled is fantastic, and their lamb chops are among the best you’ll ever have. 986

El Falah (https://maps.app.goo.gl/J8SNESB1GY87kUVBA) - When Egyptians think about Alexandria food, one of the things everyone thinks about is liver sandwich, and this place is legendary. Price - 52 EGP ($1.03) for 4 sandwiches

Welcome to Aswan, Egypt, in southern Egypt or in Upper Egypt as it’s referred to as. And today we’ll be going on an Egyptian food tour to eat some of the best food you must try when you’re in Aswan. From a man who serves fresh Nile fish as the Pharaohs ate, to home cooked Nubian food, we are in for a delicious adventure today in Egypt! 

Egyptian Breakfast at El Manayea - But first, you can’t start your day in Egypt without the staples, and I’m talking about fuul and falafel. Here they mix the fuul with hard boiled eggs and flaxseed oil, and we needed the energy for the day. 

Temple of Philae - Of course, when you’re in Aswan, there’s no way can miss the amazing sightseeing, and so after breakfast we headed to the Temple of Philae, one of the most picturesque ancient Egyptian temples on an island in the Nile River. 

Fisher Man Island (https://maps.app.goo.gl/xJVKBTU4b3EwarDR9) - Next up we went to a restaurant called Fisher Man Island where he fishes and grills and fries fish on an island rock in the Nile River. Although we didn’t have much luck fishing this time, luckily he had some pre-caught fish. We had tilapia and the highlight was a Nile Perch, a fish that was eaten by ancient Egyptian Pharaohs! 

Wanas Kato (https://maps.app.goo.gl/KhZu6LdRundu5dhP7) - Another highlight of the Egyptian food tour today was having a home-cooked Nubian food meal at our guest house. Nubians are an ethnic people group from Southern Egypt and Northern Sudan who have a rich cultural heritage and delicious food. The meal was outstanding. 

Al Masry (https://maps.app.goo.gl/euknJrFopSW69cAy9) - Finally, we’re finishing off this Aswan food tour by going to the best Egyptian bbq restaurant in Aswan.

On our Egyptian Food tour today in Cairo we’ll be eating a crazy breakfast of champions, visiting the Pyramids, and eating at a few of the best Egyptian restaurants. This is going to be a day of unforgettable Egyptian food!

Pyramids of Giza - Of course you can’t visit Egypt without going to the Pyramids of Giza, arguably one of the most iconic sights on earth? Nothing can prepare you for 4,500 years of history right before your eyes. Price - 700 EGP ($13.82) per person

Hawawshi El Rabea (https://maps.app.goo.gl/J5N2Vx7NAi7TBhnq7) - Hawawshi is one of the most beloved and greatest Egyptian street foods, and at Hawawshi El Rabea they serve you more than just hawawshi, it’s an entire theatrical performance! Price - 640 EGP ($12.63 USD) for everything

Bebo Restaurant (https://maps.app.goo.gl/GoRPfogBvcLrXgRx5) - Finally Abanoub took me to what he said is his favorite restaurant in Cairo, Bebo Restaurant that specializes in Egyptian tagines, which are slow cooked stews in earthenware pots cooked in an oven. You can get many different combinations, and I guarantee this will be one of the best restaurants you eat at in Cairo for Egyptian food! 

This was another absolutely mouthwatering and breathtaking day of Egyptian food in Cairo!

Huge thank you to my friend Abanoub for helping me arrange this tour!

Foul Wehid (https://maps.app.goo.gl/7TiuFveHtJLiinBA7) - We’re starting with an Egyptian breakfast of champions, and you won’t believe the variety and deliciousness of Egyptian breakfast on the streets of Cairo.

Kebab Muhammed El Rafey (https://maps.app.goo.gl/X4GtpUCyefvDJiec6) - Egyptians grill meat on another level and Kebab Muhammed El Rafey serves some of the best kebabs, kofta, and tarb in all of Cairo!

Bangkok, Thailand, is a lesser known world burger capital, and today we’re going to eat and review some of the best burgers in Bangkok, Thailand! First, a few rules of this tour - we’re going to try a variety of different burgers - there’s no control, so mainly we’ll try the signature burger or most popular burger at each spot. And finally, everything included in this video is a local burger from Thailand, no international chains. 

1. Daniel Thaiger Burger (https://maps.app.goo.gl/KecuadySghiMnv6S9) - A pioneer in Bangkok’s best burger scene since 2013, Daniel Thaiger Burger still serves one of the best burgers in Bangkok. I got the legendary Mr. Steve (Double). Price - 340 THB ($9.99)
BONUS - Don’t miss STAX Burger - their smashburger variety, which is outstanding. 
 
2. Bulldog Burgers & Beers (https://maps.app.goo.gl/vN6Aue1vPkx2pktX6) - This friendly burger joint in Bang Na serves American style burgers with Thai wagyu beef. I got their Oklahoma Onion Burger (Double). Price - 320 THB ($9.41) 

3. Barney's Burger Joint (https://maps.app.goo.gl/GNdbdC8n1tZrDGq1A) - Sometimes there’s nothing more satisfying than a smashburger and if you’re looking for the best smashburger in Bangkok, don’t miss the Double Trucker at Barney's Burger Joint. Price - 290 THB ($8.53)

4. Beast & Butter: Burgers & Beers (https://maps.app.goo.gl/fjRXaTiYqmvCHi6Z9) - Started as a food truck in Chiang Mai, their branch is Bangkok is higher end, and it’s without a doubt one of the highest quality burgers in Bangkok. I ate the Double Double. Price - 380 THB ($11.16)

5. Homeburg (https://maps.app.goo.gl/FMM2amMgBUEMsAWu5) - Meet Taiki Rattanapong, at his restaurant Homeburg where he serves you a “burger omakase” meal that’s unlike anything else on earth. The Homeburg Prototype #1 is one of the most delicious burgers you might ever try, and you will love his passion and precision. Price - 3,500 THB ($102.77) for entire meal

So when you’re in Thailand, don’t miss out on trying the best burgers in Bangkok!

In this Thai street food tour we’re on a mission to find the best crispy pork belly (Moo Krob หมูกรอบ) in Bangkok! But the challenge is, for every place we go, we need to try a different Thai dish that’s made using Thai style crispy pork belly. Get ready, because I’m going to show you all the spots, and every dish we try! 

Kuay Jab Mr. Joe (ก๋วยจั๊บมิสเตอร์โจ) (https://maps.app.goo.gl/x4q8L2xhNsFNqn8eA) - This place is legendary and historical, open for generations and has received many awards. Their famous dish is Kuay Jab (ก๋วยจั๊บ), a Thai Chinese noodle roll soup, loaded with some of Bangkok’s best crispy pork belly. Price - 70 THB ($2.07) 

Hom Dee Noodles (หอมดีหมี่เกี๊ยว) (https://maps.app.goo.gl/bKyzEmPkYrKMjUsj6) - Next dish we’re off to Yaowarat (Chinatown) to eat Bamee Giew Moo Krob (บะหมี่หมูกรอบ), and we’ll also see how they make their incredible version of moo krob. Price - 65 THB ($1.93)
 
Crispy Pork Alley (Aunt Tiw) (ตรอกหมูกรอบ (ป้าติ๋ว) (https://maps.app.goo.gl/utbHakcwMniWPyS38 ) - Next up on this Thai street food tour we’re going to eat Kaprao Moo Krob (กะเพราหมูกรอบ 80 THB ($2.37), crispy pork belly fried with holy basil - perhaps one of the ultimate Thai comfort foods in the world. And I couldn’t resist their Kana Moo Krob (คะน้าหมูกรอบ) - 80 THB ($2.37) as well!  

Racha Bamee Moo Krob Papa 90 Decibels (ราชาบะหมี่ (หมูกรอบปะป๊า 90 เดซิเบล https://maps.app.goo.gl/RQcdCHTpQCDVkEG2A) - This Bangkok street food stalls claims the crispiness from their pork skin is equal to 90 Decibels! And I tried their Ba Mee Yam Moo Krob (บะหมี่หมูกรอบยำแซ่บ), egg noodles with crispy pork belly salad. Price - 70 THB ($2.07)
 
Hia Tee Bang Kruai (เฮียตี๋ ช.บางกรวย) (https://maps.app.goo.gl/A5cHSEK6LxeusEBd6 ) - Finally let’s go meet the king of crispy pork belly, and see how they are able to make their crispy pork belly so insanely crispy. I tried their Khao Moo Krob (ข้าวหมูกรอบ), straight up rice and crispy pork belly. Price - 70 THB ($2.07)

Get ready for the ultimate Chinese street food tour documentary in the Shaanxi province of China! From the bustling historical streets of Xi’an to the spicy numbing Chinese food of Hanzhong we’re on a mission to eat the best and most unique Chinese food that you’re not going to want to miss. 

Arrival - We’re landing at Xi’an airport and heading straight to eat some world class dumplings - some of the best dumplings ever. 

Day 1 - We’re jumping straight into an ultimate Chinese street food tour to uncover the most unique and tasty Chinese foods in Xi’an - from famous hand pulled noodles to chive pockets and the legendary Xi’an burgers. 

Day 2 - We’ll start the day with an impressive Chinese breakfast and then proceed to eating biang biang noodles and a whole fried gourd chicken. 

Day 3 - You might know Shaanxi province from the Terracotta Army, and we aren’t going to miss it. But first we’ll have a mutton soup jacuzzi, and then taste some more amazing Chinese biang biang noodles. 

Day 4 - Today we’re jumping on the train to visit Hanzhong, a city halfway between Xi’an and Chengdu that’s known for spicy mouth numbing chili oil. We’ll find some of the most unique street food snacks and try fish swimming in chili oil. 

Day 5 - About a 3 hour drive from Xi’an and we’ll be in the beautiful mountainous countryside. There’s a hidden gem restaurant, most like a farm house, that specializes in braised rooster. 

Day 6 - Today we’re back in the heart of Xi’an where we’ll try a legendary historical restaurant for Shaanxi cuisine (including gourd chicken), and we’ll try two variations of the popular liangpi noodles, and some lamb dumplings!

Menuderia Chela (https://maps.app.goo.gl/oooNEw6EXyvsRJFR7) - Next up at the market you’ll find this incredibly popular stall that specializes in Jalisco style menudo, or stomach stew.  

Carnes Asadas Ramón (https://maps.app.goo.gl/SmeJApriqckdARZAA) - Finally right next door don’t miss Carnes Asadas Ramón for grilled beef stuffed into bread or tortillas, drenched in bean soup, and topped with fresh cream and cheese. Enfrijoladas are something you have to try! 

Basílica de Nuestra Señora de Zapopan - Next up we’re continuing with our Mexican street food tour in Zapopan, the city adjacent to Guadalajara and part of the metro area. We tried some Camote Enmielado (the sweet potatoes). 

Taqueria Santa Fe del Güero (https://maps.app.goo.gl/bgCx7jvbqSySG5Bb7) - With night, Mexico bring a whole new wave of street food, and we’re starting with Tacos de paladar (palate or roof of the mouth tacos) and tacos de lengua (tongue tacos).

Tacos Pablo Zapopan (https://maps.app.goo.gl/UEtxtTKHkbmdmUmN7) - Next stop on this food tour is tacos de carnaza!

Tripitas Don Ramón (https://maps.app.goo.gl/AT77HuSiGZuSWyZx5) - After a long and incredible day eating our way through Guadalajara we tried one of the local favorites, intestines fried in a bubble bath of their own oil, then drenched in tomato soup - something you have to try in Guadalajara!

In this video we’re going on an Omani food tour in Salalah, in the southern Dhofar region of Oman! We’re starting with a traditional celebration food of the Dhofar region, that called Madhbi, where they take an entire goat, and grill it fresh on hot rocks. The cooking process is incredible and it’s an ancient desert bbq method. The meat was so fresh and cooked perfectly with natural smoke embedded into every bite. Many locals also like to eat their meat with a dip of sweet local honey for a sweet touch. 

We’ll continue this Arabian food tour with camels, which are the lifeline in this region of Oman. We’ll learn to milk camels, very unique, and then drink camel milk as fresh as it gets! Next we’ll try Dhofari bread, another old tradition, baked in below ground overs. It’s crispy and slightly sweet, and incredibly tasty. 

Finally to complete our Omani food tour today we’re eating late night street food, and this time not only the amazing camel mishkak of Salalah, but also - you guessed it - a camel burger!

Thank you to Ahmed, Oman Travel & Tourism. Follow him: https://www.instagram.com/officialomantravels/ and his tours: https://rihlati.org/   

Also a huge thank you to Ali for taking us around Salalah!

Nizwa is an ancient city in Oman, known especially for the Nizwa Fort, history, dates, palm tree oasis, and unique food. Today we’ll be walking around and exploring Nizwa, Oman, and discovering why this city is worth visiting. 

Thank you to Ahmed, Oman Travel & Tourism. Follow him: https://www.instagram.com/officialomantravels/ and his tours: https://rihlati.org/   

Al Gatheeb Oman Sweets - One of the most famous Omani traditional sweets is halfway, and everyone loves it. It’s a combination of sugar and starch melted down with spices, nuts, and ghee, and stirred for 4 hours. The texture is so soft of pillowy and melts in your mouth with the flavor of saffron and cardamom. It’s really an art, and something extremely special you have to try in Oman. 

Nizwa Fort - This was totally unexpected, but at the Nizwa Fort we met with Mohsin Ambusaidi, who not only took us for an amazing tour, but also invited us to have a home-cooked lunch right at the fort. It was an unforgettable experience! 

Al Aqur Restaurant - Next up on this Omani food tour in Nizwa, we had lunch number two. 

Omani Street Food - In the evening, you’ll find some of the best Omani street food in Nizwa in the parking lot just outside the old city. We tried a number of local soups, snacks, and definitely some camel mishkak!

MUSCAT, OMAN - Today we’re going on an ultimate Arabian seafood tour in Muscat, Oman! Oman is blessed with an incredible coastline, and fish and seafood is a huge part of the Omani food culture. Today we’ll visit the vibrant fish market, eat at a few unique Omani seafood restaurants, and then go to Mohammed’s house to cook! 

Ahmed, Oman Travel & Tourism. Follow him: https://www.instagram.com/officialomantravels/ and his tours: https://rihlati.org/   

Follow Mohammed’s videos: @Chefjjskitchen and https://www.instagram.com/chefjjskitchen/ 

Seeb Fish Market - We’re starting this Omani seafood tour at the Seeb Fish Market, one of the most vibrant fish market, located just outside the center of Muscat. You’ll find all the fresh catch of the day, and we found amazing king fish, one of the Omani favorites and tuna.

Shrimps Restaurant‎ (https://maps.app.goo.gl/bc5yb9GWgV5tr2ZA6) - After the fish market we headed to a local seafood restaurant. At this spot you can choose all your own seafood and they will cook it fresh, marinated in Omani spices and showered in tangy tamarind.

Mohammed’s - Next up, we had the privilege to hang out with Mohammed as he cooked his version of paplou - an Omani fish and turmeric soup. 

Bab Salum Barbecue (https://maps.app.goo.gl/BZoC4jSpvMW4JwaY8) - It wouldn’t be a complete day in Oman without eating mishkak, but while mutton is common, one of the best skewers of mishkak is squid!

OMAN - I’m in Oman and today we’re heading into the desert to meet up with Badar, a local Bedouin who’s going to cook us a whole lamb shuwa, cook underground in the sand. The process is amazing to watch and the final lamb over rice is something totally unique and surprisingly delicious. It’s going to be an Omani food adventure! 

Huge thank you to Ahmed, Oman Travel & Tourism for taking us on this adventure. Follow him: https://www.instagram.com/officialomantravels/  

Follow Badar: https://www.instagram.com/albadri_bedouincamp/

To begin this lamb shuwa Omani food adventure we set off driving into the desert from Muscat. Once we reached the edge of the sand dunes we transferred to a 4x4 and into the sand dunes where we met Badar. He’s going to prepare for us a whole lamb, cooked shuwa style - which is one of the ultimate best dishes of Oman and a celebration of a meal. But Badar’s Bedouin desert version of Shuwa is different than other parts of the country. His family recipe included spices and dates marinated over the lamb, then baked in hot sand for a few hours. The result was mind blowing, so good that Ahmed and I couldn’t believe it!

We’ll have a huge breakfast, try Omani sweets, eat arsiya and madbhi with rice at a popular local restaurant, and finally eat the greatest of all Omani street foods - mishkak and the shuwa burger. 

Huge thank you to Ahmed, Oman Travel & Tourism for taking us around Oman. Follow Ahmed: https://www.instagram.com/officialomantravels/ 

Rozna Restaurant (https://maps.app.goo.gl/EGC6EZEPGanM9fqB9) - We’re starting this Omani food tour at one of the best restaurants in Muscat. We tried Omani bread, fried liver, and a bunch of other Omani dishes. We also happened to meet the manager Sulaiman Alkindi, who gave us a full tour of the restaurant, and also let us sample the lamb shuwa right out of the underground oven. Total price - 11 OMR ($28.53)

Al Diwaniya Omani Sweets (https://maps.app.goo.gl/agqaVasvpd1oGnbk7) - Next up Ahmed took me to try Omani halwa, a dessert that’s also an Omani traditional celebration!
